overview: White plays 1.d3 and 2.Nd2, a Reversed Philidor set-up that prepares e4, Ngf3 and a slow development without committing the c- and g-pawns. Black can seize the centre with ...d5 and ...Nf6, so White usually answers with e4 and Be2 or g3 to keep a flexible, slightly cramped position. There is little theory and the game is more about manoeuvring than early tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Prepare e4 with Nd2 and Ngf3
Develop with g3/Bg2 or Be2 and castle
Keep a compact position and wait for the centre to take shape

black_ideas.idea: Develop freely and aim for ...Bc5 or ...Be7
Challenge White's centre with ...f5 or ...c5 depending on White's set-up

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Philidor with White pawns on d3, e4
King's Indian Attack-like set-ups with g3 and Bg2

character.notes: Slow, manoeuvring play where neither side is under early pressure; hard to lose but also hard to play for a win.

soundness.notes: Sound and playable; not a refuted opening.

structure.notes: Centre is not decided early: tension and later pawn breaks.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom start with 1.d3 and 2.Nd2; chosen mainly to avoid theory.

level.notes: Needs middlegame understanding; little to memorise.

character.reason: Quiet development with a compact pawn structure.

approach.reason: Rarely chosen by strong players over main-line openings; could be read as a system.

level.reason: Plans matter more than moves, but the set-up is not trivial.

plans.reason: No plan is plainly characteristic from memory.
